details: Global risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, experienced a sharp decline following renewed tensions in the Middle East. On May 28, 2026, US airstrikes on Iran led to immediate investor concerns over escalating regional conflict. Bitcoin fell below $73,000, and Ethereum dipped to $1,974. This geopolitical uncertainty, coupled with broader macro caution and outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs, contributed to the synchronized market pressure.
title: US-Iran Strikes Lead to Crypto Market Downturn

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) warned on May 27, 2026, of significant financial stability risks stemming from the intensifying Middle East conflict. The ECB's Financial Stability Review highlighted that ongoing geopolitical tensions and energy supply disruptions are pushing inflation higher and could undermine confidence in financial markets. ECB Vice-President Luis de Guindos noted that a more persistent energy shock could lead to weaker growth and abrupt repricing in sovereign bond markets, impacting borrowing costs and fiscal sustainability.
title: ECB Flags Middle East Conflict's Impact on Eurozone Financial Stability
